digest.component_or_area: LLM prompt caching across plan-review passes
propositions: Prompt cache breakpoints are placed after pass-specific stance suffixes instead of at the byte-stable shared_plan_prefix boundary, causing zero cache reads across passes within a single run despite byte-identical leading content.

Cache writes incur premium billing (1.25x) on every plan-review gate call while reads receive discount (0.1x), but single-call passes write once and never read, wasting ~5k token-equivalents per review through premium-write premium with zero benefit.

The marked prefix embeds the full plan by design for within-run container/chunk reuse (warm-then-fan-out), so content-addressed caching cannot reuse a prefix across different tickets; the Phase-1 AC requiring cross-ticket byte-identity is unsatisfiable without destroying within-run reuse.
The ineffective-cache diagnostic only fires when both write==0 and read==0, leaving the write-every-call/read-0 shape invisible; telemetry must separately detect and flag this costly pattern.

Relocating the cache breakpoint to the end of the shared_plan_prefix (via RunRequest.cache_prefix as a runner-seam knob, sending prefix as static system_prompt and remainder as dynamic instruction) allows the finder write to be read by Pass-2 verifiers within one run and same-ticket re-reviews within TTL.
Reordering prerequisite_verifier template to lead with {{shared_prefix}} restores fidelity while enabling the shared-prefix breakpoint read path.
